newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke to address parliament on EMU on Monday.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke to address parliament on EMU on Monday.

text.p: British Chancellor Kenneth Clarke will make a statement to parliament on Monday about the European single currency, a Treasury statement said on Sunday.

"In view of the highly misleading and inaccurate article in the Sunday Times today about single currency issues, the Chancellor of the Exchequer will make a statement to the House of Commons tomorrow afternoon," the statement said.

The Sunday Times reported that crucial documents concerning preparations for a single European currency had been kept from members of parliament. The reports suggested that the pound will be required to shadow the Euro even if it does not enter a new exchange rate mechanism, the paper said.

"(Clarke) will take the opportunity to correct that and other misleading reports that have emerged over recent days, to reiterate the points in his letter to MPs and spell out the government's position on the issues under discussion at the Ecofin council on December 2 and at the European Council in Dublin," the Treasury statement said.
Pro-European politicians and Eurosceptics alike have called for a full parliamentary debate on EMU before Clarke attends the Ecofin meeting of European Union finance ministers early next month.
For Clarke to address parliament just one day before his annual budget is highly unusual. The Chancellor would usually adopt a pre-budget purdah scrupulously.
